Rules s3 puts reject and reopen under 'Moving a card', and Undo 'gives back a rejection reason the move removed' only makes sense if reopen (hence reject) is a move; the hro_reject_reason and hro_reopen undo legs follow that single reading. (b) Stale-replay ABA in protocol C (F Applied->Screen, Mei Screen->Applied, replay): an app keying staleness on from-stage would accept the replay, but rules s3 states 'every card carries a version that changes whenever the card moves', so version-based refusal is the stated contract. (c) Observer/candidate undo replay status: rules s1 makes a role refusal 403 regardless of 'nothing to undo'; golden workspace.cjs:123 does so. (d) Functional B(12) 're-order a different J2 card (Y)': with Y at the top of Screen (Y,W,X,Z,A2) a one-place ordinary re-order cannot displace A2, so an app that also bumps versions of displaced siblings still lets the undo go ahead; only a multi-place drag of Y below A2 would open a second reading (P3, latent). (2) A sign-out control is implied, not named: instruction.md:7 'get signed out ... nobody else who signs in on that browser' and polish hro_pol_session_resume rely on it. (3) Note-draft privacy from another user (hro_pol_session_resume) rests on rules s3 'keep it for me on that browser'; reasonable but less explicit than s6 for replies.
